items.text: The process that loads DAILY_LOC_FUEL_F was not found in the available material, nor was anything referencing its distinctive per-pump file naming

A change to the loading process happened on 2025-10-09: the source file name and three cumulative figures (weekly, monthly and year-to-date gallons pumped) stopped being recorded on every row since, including today. Only the daily figures are still populated. Confirmed row by row, not just by matching counts: zero rows in the entire table have one of these fields populated without the others

No formal unique business key is enforced on this table, unlike most tables in this project. A plausible natural combination of columns holds with no duplicates in the data, but nothing in the table's own structure enforces it

This table's two formal links to other tables are both named after a different table name than this one. This strongly suggests the table was renamed at some point and the old links were never renamed with it
One row out of 4.49 million carries an invalid internal key, dated 2018

A related file confirms a named external data connection is used for more than one fuel/loyalty integration in this environment, including a similar report for a different partner program, but that file does not write to this table

blocks.text: Still open, not confirmed in code or data yet. None of this blocks the lineage above, it is tracked here so nothing gets forgotten.

items.text: What system actually loads DAILY_LOC_FUEL_F has not been identified. The table is clearly live and receiving new data, but nothing in the available material writes to it
items.note: The source appears to be a per-store daily file drop, a pattern seen elsewhere in this project, but no direct match was found

items.text: Whether the 2025-10-09 change that stopped recording the file name and the three cumulative gallon figures was intentional has not been confirmed
items.note: If any report still expects those three cumulative figures, it has been getting blanks for almost a year

blocks.text: A few things below are still not fully confirmed. We are sharing this table's analysis now rather than holding it back, because the rest of it is solid and these gaps are clearly called out here, not hidden.

items.text: Still unknown: who gets notified if this process fails.
items.note: We could not find the program that loads this table anywhere in the files we have, so we have no way to see who is notified if it fails.

items.text: Still unknown: whether this process runs on a set schedule.
items.note: Same root cause as alerts: without the loading program itself, we have no way to confirm how often it runs.
